text: {"memo": "McDonald’s reported FY2024, ended December 31, 2024, revenue of about $25.9 billion, up roughly 2% from $25.5 billion in FY2023. Global comparable sales rose only about 0.3% for the year, though the final quarter showed a sequential slowdown. Net income was about $10.2 billion, or diluted EPS of about $11.4, a sharp recovery from $8.5 billion and $8.2 of EPS in FY2023. Operating margin improved to roughly 47%, and net margin around 39%, from 33% in FY2023. Cash flow from operations was about $12 billion, with free cash flow around $7 billion. In FY2023, revenue was $25.5 billion, up 10% from $23.2 billion in FY2022, with global comparable sales up 9.4%. Net income was $8.5 billion and EPS $8.2. FY2022 revenue was $23.2 billion, down slightly from $23.2 billion in FY2021, but global comparable sales rose 7.1%. Net income was $6.2 billion and EPS $6.4. FY2021 revenue was $23.2 billion, up 13.5%, net income $4.5 billion and EPS $4.6. The business showed resilient pricing power and cost discipline, but growth slowed sharply from pandemic-era rebounds. View: McDonald’s is a solid franchise story, but the stock is fairly valued and vulnerable to renewed consumer weakness."}
